data.title: Western Digital Stock Falls Despite Visibility to 2031
data.description:
Western Digital reported fiscal first-quarter non-GAAP EPS of $4.64, above the analysts' consensus of $4.11, on revenue of $4.38 billion, up 55% from a year earlier and ahead of the $4.14 billion estimate. Western Digital shares fell 2.87% in premarket.

Non-GAAP gross margin widened to 58.1% from 43.9% a year earlier, and non-GAAP operating margin reached 49.1%. CFO Kris Sennesael credited robust exabyte growth and improved pricing. Free cash flow was $1.38 billion, and the company repurchased $1.0 billion of stock in the quarter. It also raised its quarterly dividend 17% to $0.175 per share.

For the fiscal second quarter, Western Digital guided revenue to $5.1 billion, plus or minus $100 million, or growth of 66% to 72% year over year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 60% to 61% and non-GAAP EPS of $5.80, plus or minus $0.20. On the earnings call, CEO Irving Tan said Western Digital has good visibility up to 2030, 2031 across its top seven customers, and that their demand signal keeps rising quarter after quarter.

data.title: ServiceNow Gets a Major Wall Street Vote of Confidence Ahead of Earnings
data.description:
ServiceNow (NOW) received a higher valuation assessment from Guggenheim, which raised its price target to $175 from $125 and retained a Buy rating. The new objective relies on a valuation of roughly 10.5 times projected recurring revenue.

Feedback from five partners suggests customers are continuing to spend on ServiceNow's software, although demand has not broadly accelerated. One partner described business as better than anticipated, while four reported performance close to their expectations. Guggenheim believes this environment supports the company's prospects for meeting third-quarter estimates for growth in contracted work awaiting revenue recognition.

The brokerage also sees the company's core IT service-management business supporting sales momentum. Its partners reported healthy pipelines, while Guggenheim expects management's guidance for the following quarter to be at least in line with market forecasts.

ServiceNow's strategy of incorporating artificial intelligence features into product packages has received differing reactions. Some partners observed increased usage and said customers were finding it easier to assess potential returns. Others said the new pricing structure had caused dissatisfaction among buyers. Overall adoption of AI offerings remains at an early stage, though two partners reported growing interest in AI Control Tower.

ABG Sundal Collier AB ("ABG"), in its capacity as Sole Global Coordinator and stabilisation manager, notifies that the overallotment option granted in connection with Linjemontage i Grästorp AB’s (publ) (“Linjemontage” or the “Company”) offering of existing shares in the Company and the listing of the Company's shares on Nasdaq Stockholm (the "Offering") has been partly exercised. As announced in connection with the Offering, ABG had the option, acting as Sole Global Coordinator and stabilisation manager, to carry out transactions aimed at supporting the market price of the shares at levels above those which might otherwise have prevailed in the market. Kalpataru Power Transmission Sweden AB ("Kalpataru Sweden") granted ABG an over-allotment option which could have been utilised in whole or in part for 30 calendar days from the first day of trading of the Company's shares on Nasdaq Stockholm to be able to sell up to 2,146,743 additional existing shares in the Company corresponding to up to 15 percent of the total number of shares in the Offering to cover any over-allotment in connection with the Offering.

ABG now notifies that the over-allotment option has been exercised corresponding to 1,877,911 shares. Thus, the remaining part of the over-allotment option that was not exercised, corresponding to 268,832 shares, will be returned to Kalpataru Sweden.

About Linjemontage

Linjemontage is a Swedish pure-play EPC provider within power infrastructure, enabling the modernisation and expansion of the electricity grid in Sweden and Norway. With over three decades of experience, the Company has established one of the leading positions in Sweden in terms of market share and profitability. Linjemontage is one of few EPC providers in Sweden focused exclusively on energy, delivering projects within substations and transmission and distribution networks across the full voltage range. Its customers include national transmission system operators such as Svenska kraftnät and Statnett, regional distribution companies such as Ellevio, Vattenfall Eldistribution and E.ON, and industrial customers such as Volvo and LKAB, as well as data centres.

The Company is active in two principal areas of power infrastructure: substations, and transmission and distribution networks. Its portfolio spans both newbuild projects and refurbishment of existing assets. Linjemontage has extensive experience in designing and constructing substations up to 400 kV and believes it is among the few contractors that can deliver cable projects up to 400 kV. Typical substation and transmission projects range from approximately SEK 50 million to SEK 500 million, while larger transmission projects sometimes exceed SEK 500 million.

Founded in 1993, Linjemontage has gradually evolved from a regional grid services provider into a specialised Swedish EPC contractor operating in the electricity grid market in Sweden and Norway with strong high-voltage capabilities. The Company operates from 19 offices in Sweden, two in Norway and one in Croatia, and has recently established an operation centre in India expected to provide engineering support to projects in Sweden and Norway. In 2024, Linjemontage won its largest project to date, a transmission project for Svenska kraftnät valued at approximately SEK 1 billion, followed in 2026 by a 400 kV substation project for Svenska kraftnät valued at approximately SEK 779 million.

For the financial year ended 31 March 2026, Linjemontage's net sales amounted to SEK 3,225 million, with an adjusted EBITA of SEK 245 million, corresponding to an adjusted EBITA margin of 7.6 percent. As of 30 June 2026, the Company had an order book of SEK 4,349 million.

data.title: SKYD Stock Gets JPMorgan Upgrade: Analyst Sees Skydance Gaining Ground On Netflix, Disney With Warner Bros. Deal
data.description:
Key points:
  • JPMorgan resumed coverage of Skydance on Friday, upgrading the stock to ‘Neutral’ from ‘Underweight’.
  • It lowered its price target to $9, down from $14, in line with the Wall Street average.
  • Wall Street largely remains cautious on SKYD stock with nine of the 23 analysts that cover the stock giving it a ‘Sell’ or ‘Strong Sell’ rating and 10 recommending ‘Hold’.

Skydance (SKYD) shares were little changed in midday trade on Friday after JPMorgan upgraded the stock, citing that its Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition creates a media company larger by revenue than Netflix (NFLX) and Disney (DIS) excluding theme parks.

In a note to investors cited by TheFly, JPMorgan resumed coverage of Skydance, upgrading it to ‘Neutral’ from ‘Underweight’. However, the firm lowered its price target to $9, down from $14, leaving a potential upside of almost 15% from current levels.

SKYD stock edged around 0.5% lower in midday trade. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the shares improved to ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’ territory over the past day.

JPMorgan Sees Streaming, Cost-Saving Opportunities From Warner Deal 

JPMorgan said Skydance’s scale creates opportunities to improve content monetization, cross-sell its streaming services and remove duplicated costs.

After the acquisition, Skydance now owns Paramount and Warner Bros., HBO, CBS and CNN, along with the Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming services. Management says the company generates nearly $70 billion in annual revenue.

JPMorgan’s assessment echoes priorities outlined by Skydance’s co-CEOs in a CNBC interview earlier this month. Chairman and CEO David Ellison said the company plans to combine its two streaming services, which he expects would give the business more than 200 million subscribers.

Ellison also identified five priorities for the combined company, including mid-single-digit revenue growth, integrating the streaming platforms, expanding the studio and direct-to-consumer businesses, and upgrading the company’s technology and operating platforms.

Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz said Skydance expects to realize about one-third of its $6 billion synergy target in the first year. He added that labor costs would not account for most of the anticipated savings. “We have a clear vision and line of sight to achieve the savings we’re aiming towards,” he said.

Wall Street Remains Cautious On SKYD Stock

JPMorgan’s $9 target is in line with Wall Street’s 12-month average target as per Koyfin data. However, ratings suggest that more analysts are cautious than bullish on SKYD stock. Only four out of the 23 analysts covering the stock give it a ‘Buy’ or ‘Strong Buy’ rating, with 10 recommending ‘Hold’ and 9 recommending ‘Sell’ or ‘Strong Sell’.

Other firms have also taken a cautious view of the company’s prospects since the merger closed. Bernstein SocGen cut its price target to $6 from $12 last week while maintaining an ‘Underperform’ rating. The firm said Skydance was “very much a show me story with considerable execution risk in the years ahead.”

Meanwhile, Morningstar lowered its fair value estimate to $12 from $15 after about 471 million warrants began trading. Barclays has an ‘Underweight’ rating and a $7 target.

Investors are also assessing the capital behind the transaction and the company’s financial outlook. The Ellison family reportedly contributed about $17 billion toward financing the deal, purchasing an estimated 1.4 billion shares at $12 apiece. Semafor reported Thursday that Elon Musk invested about $1 billion in Skydance.

Meanwhile, media mogul John Malone said Wednesday that he expects Musk’s SpaceX (SPCX) to invest $8 billion to $10 billion in the company.

Skydance is scheduled to report its first earnings since the acquisition on November 9. Wall Street is expecting earnings per share (EPS) of $0.19 on revenue of around $7 billion.

data.title: EU vows to fix 'China Shock 2.0' via talks with Beijing
data.description:
Key points:
  • Plastics safeguards probe appears closest to launch, Sefcovic says
  • Goods trade deficit with China exceeds €1 billion a day
  • EU agreed with Beijing to halve vehicle imports from China

By Philip Blenkinsop and Padraic Halpin

The European Union should focus on dialogue with Beijing to curb imports of products such as chemicals and machinery to rein in a damaging trade deficit with China, EU ministers said on Friday, as the bloc considers import quotas for plastics.

European Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic earlier this month agreed with Beijing for the EU to cut imports of hybrid vehicles from China by more than half to address a deficit that has swelled to more than €1 billion ($1.12 billion) a day, and to support Europe's struggling carmakers.

Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee told a news conference after a ministerial meeting in Dublin that all EU members were determined the Commission should continue dialogue with Beijing

"There's a very clear desire for us to move beyond that (hybrid cars) and to look at other areas, chemicals, machinery. There's a number of issues, agrifood sector, and areas that have been mentioned," she said.

She added that, while dialogue was the priority, the Commission could use existing trade defence tools itself to resolve some imbalances.

Sefcovic told the news conference he had heard every trade minister's views on which sectors should be the next priorities for trade measures.

PLASTICS SAFEGUARDS NEXT IN LINE

He continued that an investigation into safeguards for plastics appeared to be the next to be launched.

"Currently, I think the plastics sector is the closest," he said. "We are looking into whether all the requirements to launch an investigation are in place."

He appeared to be referring to a request for measures to curb imports of PET, the plastic widely used in packaging, which lawyers told Reuters earlier this month had been submitted.

China needs foreign buyers for the flood of relatively cheap state-subsidised goods its own shoppers can't absorb, and the EU is torn between welcoming those imports to ease living costs and keeping them out to rebuild its own factories.

The EU's goods trade deficit swelled to more than €370 billion ($414.25 billion) in 2025 and is on course to break well past €400 billion this year, a situation European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has called "unsustainable".

European industry says the export surge, dubbed China Shock 2.0, is already causing factory closures and job losses, most notably the 100,000 positions set to go at Volkswagen.

China has said in the past it is not the root cause of the EU's problems, but a partner in solving them.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said this week there were growing concerns for chemicals and machinery. Lithuania Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said on Friday that pharmaceuticals could also be included.

France's junior minister for trade, Nicolas Forissier, said dialogue was only possible now that the EU was speaking as one.

Chinese authorities "understand when you are clear, when you speak frankly, when you are firm on your positions," he said.

($1 = 0.8914 euros)

data.title: Stocks mixed, day after AI-related selloff; oil prices rise again
data.description:
Key points:
  • Wall Street stocks mostly lower
  • Oil prices extend recent gains
  • US Treasury yields up; France gets respite

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Marc Jones

Stock indexes were mixed on Friday, with tech shares edging higher after the previous day's selloff, while Brent crude oil rose to its highest in more than five months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.

The Nasdaq was up 0.2% after starting the day lower, while the Dow was last down about 1%.

An index of semiconductors was up about 1%. It posted its biggest daily percentage drop since June on Thursday after a report from Meta Platforms reignited worries about the AI trade.

It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth in Boston.

"After Meta's report, there's still anxiety over the AI trade to a certain extent," he said. "But also, we continue to be in a place where things look like they're getting worse, not better, in the Middle East. That moves energy prices higher, which is obviously going to end up being a significant headwind for economic activity."

Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia fanned fears over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where United Arab Emirates authorities also reported an oil spill.

US crude rose 2.56% to $102.02 a barrel and Brent climbed to $116.27 per barrel, up 2.74%. European natural gas prices jumped.

AMEX, TELECOM SHARES FALL

Investors were digesting corporate earnings news. American Express shares fell 3.5% after it reported results and its CEO said the company had good momentum, but needed to become a more "agile and efficient" organization.

Telecom company shares, including Verizon , dropped after a Bloomberg News report that SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 476.25 points, or 0.9%, to 52,391.73, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX eased 11.14 points, or 0.14%, to 7,652.96 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 52.51 points, or 0.21%, to 26,062.75.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI fell 1.64 points, or 0.15%, to 1,121.29.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.4%.

Asia's bourses steadied overnight, with South Korea's KOSPI ending its session higher after shedding as much as 4% earlier.

US Treasury yields rose a day after the benchmark 10-year yield registered its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years, but remained under 5%.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last up 3.7 basis points at 4.992%. The 10-year yield is down about 11 basis points on the week and on pace for a third straight week of declines, its longest run lower since June.

EURO FALLS

The euro fell and was on track for a weekly loss against both the US dollar and the yen, while euro zone bonds stabilized after recent volatility. Investors' focus has been on concerns over France's finances.

French yields (FR10YT=RR), which were down 5 basis points at 5.04%, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, the most of any major euro zone country and the most in a week since late May.

A selloff in French government bonds this week pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011.

France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said. The country faces the threat of a rating downgrade by Moody’s later on Friday.

The euro was last down 0.12% at $1.12 , set to end the week 0.35% lower.

data.title: Midterm Elections Could Have Meaningful Impact on Yields — Market Talk
data.description: The outlook for Treasury yields "is highly dependent on Middle East conflict, Ukraine, Russia [and] potentially midterms," DWS's George Catrambone says. Catrambone says the pace of investment on artificial intelligence infrastructure can also be affected by the midterms. Given the uncertainties, his investment strategy is "to be nimble." Catrambone likes high-grade corporate bonds that are trading at a discount, while selectively adding lower quality yields aiming at a "strongly yielding portfolio and one that is diversified." data.title: Corn, soy basis bids mostly steady-stronger
data.description:
Spot basis bids for corn and soybeans were mostly steady to stronger in the US Midwest on Friday, reflecting demand from grain handlers as a weeks-long slide in Chicago Board of Trade corn futures curbed farmer selling and the soybean harvest neared completion in some areas, merchandisers said.

  • The spot corn basis firmed by 4 to 5 cents a bushel at ethanol plants in Illinois and Iowa, and by a penny at a Cincinnati, Ohio, elevator.

  • The corn basis improved by 1 to 5 cents at two Midwest river elevators, where grain is loaded onto barges for shipment on the Mississippi River toward Gulf Coast exporters.

  • For soybeans, bids improved by 9 to 16 cents at two river elevators, reflecting demand from Gulf exporters following a series of US soybean sales to China since mid-October.

  • However, the soybean basis weakened by 5 cents at a Toledo, Ohio, terminal.

  • Among domestic processors, soybean bids were steady to firmer, with the basis improving by 5 cents at a Morristown, Indiana, crushing facility.

  • Some Indiana farmers were nearly finished harvesting soybeans and were moving on to corn, two grain merchandisers said this week.

  • CBOT December corn (CZ26) was down 4-1/4 cents at $4.56-1/4 per bushel in midday trading, hovering near a three-month low set on Wednesday, while November soybean futures (SX26) were up 4-3/4 cents at $12.57-3/4 a bushel, rallying from a near two-month low set this week.
